entries.title: Motion to Compel Discovery
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to compel the Commonwealth to produce all outstanding mandatory and requested discovery, including police reports, witness statements, photographs, video and audio recordings, scientific reports, identification procedure materials, electronic evidence, and all favorable evidence.
entries.relief: compelling production of all outstanding discovery

entries.title: Motion to Preserve Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth and any law enforcement agency to preserve all physical, digital, documentary, audio, video, forensic, and electronic evidence relevant to this case.
entries.relief: preserving all evidence relevant to this case

entries.title: Motion for Brady and Impeachment Material
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for disclosure of all evidence favorable to the defense, including exculpatory evidence, impeachment material, inconsistent statements, police credibility material, witness bias, inducements, promises, benefits, and information affecting witness perception, memory, or truthfulness.
entries.relief: disclosure of all Brady and impeachment material

entries.title: Motion to Enforce Prior Discovery Orders
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to enforce this Court's prior discovery orders and to require immediate compliance by the Commonwealth.
entries.relief: enforcing prior discovery orders and requiring immediate compliance

entries.title: Motion for Sanctions for Discovery Noncompliance
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for sanctions due to the Commonwealth's failure to comply with discovery obligations, including exclusion of evidence, continuance, adverse instruction, or such other relief as justice requires.
entries.relief: imposing sanctions for discovery noncompliance
authorities: Commonwealth v. Labillios, 95 Mass. App. Ct. 1106 (2019)

entries.title: Motion for Additional Discovery
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for additional discovery because the requested materials are relevant and necessary to investigation, motion practice, trial preparation, impeachment, or development of a defense.
entries.relief: compelling production of additional discovery

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Stop
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence obtained as a result of an unlawful stop because police lacked reasonable suspicion that the Defendant had committed, was committing, or was about to commit a crime.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence obtained as a result of the unlawful stop

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Frisk
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence obtained from the frisk because police lacked a reasonable belief that the Defendant was armed and dangerous.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence obtained from the unlawful frisk

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Search
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence obtained from the search because the search was conducted without a warrant, probable cause, valid consent, or a recognized exception to the warrant requirement.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence obtained from the unlawful search
authorities: Commonwealth v. Polanco, 92 Mass. App. Ct. 764 (2018)

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Seizure
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence obtained from the unlawful seizure because police lacked reasonable suspicion, probable cause, or lawful authority to seize the Defendant or his property.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence obtained from the unlawful seizure

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Warrant Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence obtained pursuant to the warrant because the warrant was not supported by probable cause, lacked particularity, relied on stale or unreliable information, or was otherwise constitutionally defective.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence obtained pursuant to the defective warrant
authorities: Commonwealth v. Polanco, 92 Mass. App. Ct. 764 (2018)

entries.title: Motion to Challenge Probable Cause
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to challenge probable cause because the facts known to law enforcement did not justify the stop, arrest, search, seizure, warrant, or prosecution.
entries.relief: challenging probable cause and suppressing all fruits thereof
authorities: Commonwealth v. Polanco, 92 Mass. App. Ct. 764 (2018)

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Out-of-Court Identification
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress any out- of-court identification because the identification procedure was unnecessarily suggestive and created a substantial risk of misidentification.
entries.relief: suppressing all out-of-court identification evidence

entries.title: Motion to Preclude In-Court Identification
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to preclude any in- court identification where the witness did not participate in a reliable pretrial identification procedure, or where the prior procedure was suggestive, unreliable, or suppressed.
entries.relief: precluding any in-court identification testimony

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Suggestive Identification Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude identification evidence obtained through suggestive procedures, including show-ups, photo arrays, officer prompts, confirmation feedback, or other circumstances that undermined reliability.
entries.relief: excluding all suggestive identification evidence

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Lay Identification from Video
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude lay opinion identification testimony from video or images unless the Commonwealth establishes that the witness has sufficient familiarity with the Defendant and that the testimony is reliable and helpful to the factfinder.
entries.relief: excluding lay identification testimony from video or images
authorities: Commonwealth v. Meola, 95 Mass. App. Ct. 303 (2019)

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Statements - Miranda
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all statements allegedly made during custodial interrogation because the Commonwealth cannot prove valid Miranda warnings and a knowing, intelligent, and voluntary waiver.
entries.relief: suppressing all statements made during custodial interrogation
authorities: Commonwealth v. Agabalian, 97 Mass. App. Ct. 1125 (2020)

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Involuntary Statements
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all statements because they were not the product of free will and were obtained through coercion, pressure, threats, promises, deception, intoxication, language barriers, mental health issues, or other circumstances rendering them involuntary.
entries.relief: suppressing all involuntary statements
authorities: Commonwealth v. Agabalian, 97 Mass. App. Ct. 1125 (2020)

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Statements Lacking Context or Attribution
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude alleged statements that lack reliable attribution, complete context, authentication, or foundation sufficient to show that the Defendant made the statements and that they are being accurately represented.
entries.relief: excluding all statements lacking reliable attribution or context
authorities: Commonwealth v. Meola, 95 Mass. App. Ct. 303 (2019)

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Unauthenticated Screenshots
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude screenshots because the Commonwealth has not established that the screenshots are authentic, complete, unaltered, accurately attributed, or what the Commonwealth claims them to be.
entries.relief: excluding all unauthenticated screenshots
authorities: Commonwealth v. Meola, 95 Mass. App. Ct. 303 (2019)

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Social Media Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude social media posts, messages, profiles, photographs, or metadata unless the Commonwealth can authenticate the evidence and reliably link it to the Defendant.
entries.relief: excluding all unauthenticated social media evidence
authorities: Commonwealth v. Meola, 95 Mass. App. Ct. 303 (2019)

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Cell Phone Attribution Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude evidence purporting to attribute a phone, number, account, message, call, or data point to the Defendant unless the Commonwealth establishes reliable authentication and attribution.
entries.relief: excluding all cell phone attribution evidence
authorities: Commonwealth v. Meola, 95 Mass. App. Ct. 303 (2019)

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Digital Payment Attribution
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude digital payment evidence unless the Commonwealth proves that the transfer record is authentic, accurate, complete, and reliably attributable to the Defendant rather than another user or account holder.
entries.relief: excluding all digital payment attribution evidence
authorities: Commonwealth v. Meola, 95 Mass. App. Ct. 303 (2019)

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Location Data / Digital Tracking
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude location data, mapping evidence, cell-site evidence, GPS evidence, or speculative digital tracking unless the Commonwealth establishes reliability, methodology, foundation, and proper attribution.
entries.relief: excluding all location data and speculative digital tracking evidence
authorities: Commonwealth v. Meola, 95 Mass. App. Ct. 303 (2019)

entries.title: Motion in Limine to Exclude Prior Bad Acts
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude evidence of alleged prior bad acts, uncharged conduct, character evidence, or propensity evidence because such evidence is inadmissible to prove bad character or criminal disposition.
entries.relief: excluding all prior bad act and propensity evidence

entries.title: Motion in Limine to Exclude Prior Convictions
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude prior convictions unless the Commonwealth establishes a proper admissible purpose and the Court finds that any probative value is not substantially outweighed by unfair prejudice.
entries.relief: excluding prior convictions

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Gang References
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude any reference to gangs, gang membership, gang affiliation, or gang- related activity unless directly relevant to a material issue and not unfairly prejudicial.
entries.relief: excluding all gang references and gang-related evidence

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Immigration Status
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude any reference to immigration status, nationality, citizenship, deportation, visa status, or undocumented status because such evidence is irrelevant, unfairly prejudicial, and risks improper bias.
entries.relief: excluding all references to immigration status

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Firearm References Not Tied to Charged Conduct
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude any firearm references, firearm photographs, firearm allegations, or firearm- related statements not directly tied to the charged conduct.
entries.relief: excluding all firearm references not tied to the charged conduct

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Irrelevant Bad Character Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude bad character evidence, inflammatory allegations, collateral misconduct, or reputation evidence that invites the jury to convict based on character rather than proof beyond a reasonable doubt.
entries.relief: excluding all irrelevant bad character evidence

entries.title: Motion for Funds - Private Investigator (Ex Parte)
entries.theory: The Defendant moves, ex parte, for funds to retain a private investigator because investigative services are reasonably necessary to assure the Defendant as effective a defense as he would have if financially able to pay.
entries.relief: authorizing funds to retain a private investigator

entries.title: Affidavit of Counsel in Support of Motion for Funds
entries.theory: Counsel states under the pains and penalties of perjury that, based on review of the charges, procedural posture, and discovery, investigative services are reasonably necessary for preparation of the defense, including locating witnesses, interviewing witnesses, reviewing relevant locations, and developing exculpatory evidence.
entries.relief: authorizing funds as set forth in the supporting affidavit

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Breathalyzer Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence obtained from the breathalyzer test on the grounds that the test was administered in violation of applicable regulations and the Defendant's rights under the Fourth Amendment and Article 14 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights.
entries.relief: suppressing all breathalyzer evidence and any results thereof
authorities: Commonwealth v. Canavan, 40 Mass. App. Ct. 642 (1996)
Commonwealth v. Lubiejewski, 49 Mass. App. Ct. 212 (2000)

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss - Failure to Follow OUI Procedures
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss the OUI charge because the Commonwealth failed to inform the Defendant of his right to be examined by a physician of his own choosing pursuant to G.L. c. 263, § 5(a), and failed to advise of the penalties for refusing a breathalyzer test, thereby denying the Defendant potentially exculpatory evidence and violating due process.
entries.relief: dismissing the OUI charge with prejudice

entries.title: Motion for Production of BWC and CMC Footage
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth to produce full, complete, unadulterated copies of all Body Worn Camera and Cruiser Mounted Camera videos, pictures, and any other associated images related to the present case.
entries.relief: compelling production of all BWC and CMC footage

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss - Unlawful Stop
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss because the officer lacked probable cause to stop, question, and/or search the Defendant's motor vehicle. The Defendant was not committing any traffic violation at the time of the stop, in violation of the Fourth Amendment, Article 14, and M.G.L. c. 90.
entries.relief: dismissing all charges arising from the unlawful stop
authorities: Commonwealth v. Canavan, 40 Mass. App. Ct. 642 (1996)
Commonwealth v. Lubiejewski, 49 Mass. App. Ct. 212 (2000)

entries.title: Motion in Limine - Exclude Breathalyzer Results at Trial
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude breathalyzer results at trial on the grounds that the breath test results are unreliable and do not satisfy the Daubert/Lanigan standard for admissibility of scientific evidence in Massachusetts.
entries.relief: excluding all breathalyzer results from evidence at trial
authorities: Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, 509 U.S. 579 (1993)

entries.title: Motion in Limine - Exclude Field Sobriety Test Results
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude field sobriety test results from evidence at trial on the grounds that the tests were improperly administered and do not constitute reliable evidence of impairment.
entries.relief: excluding all field sobriety test results from evidence at trial

entries.title: Motion in Limine - Exclude Prior OUI Convictions
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude any prior OUI convictions from evidence during the guilt phase of trial. Prior OUI convictions are not relevant to guilt and are only admissible at sentencing for purposes of an enhanced penalty.
entries.relief: excluding all prior OUI convictions from the guilt phase of trial

entries.title: Motion in Limine - Limit Breathalyzer Refusal Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude or limit evidence of the Defendant's refusal to take a breathalyzer test and requests a limiting instruction. The probative value of refusal evidence is substantially outweighed by the danger of unfair prejudice.
entries.relief: excluding or limiting breathalyzer refusal evidence and requesting a limiting instruction

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss - Discovery Violations
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss the above- captioned matter for the Commonwealth's failure to comply with this Court's discovery order. The Commonwealth has violated this Court's order by failing to produce and/or make available for inspection or copying the evidence and reports ordered by this Court.
entries.relief: dismissing the above-captioned matter for the Commonwealth's failure to comply with discovery

entries.title: Motion for Bill of Particulars
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order directing the Commonwealth to file a bill of particulars. The indictment or complaint fails to provide sufficient detail regarding the time, place, manner, or means by which the alleged offense occurred, preventing the Defendant from having reasonable notice of the charges and impairing the ability to prepare an adequate defense.
entries.relief: ordering the Commonwealth to file a bill of particulars
authorities: Commonwealth v. Martinez, 98 Mass. App. Ct. 545

entries.title: Motion in Limine - Exclude or Limit Audio Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude or limit the admission of audio evidence proffered by the Commonwealth on the grounds that it has not been properly authenticated, is unfairly prejudicial, and is cumulative of other available evidence.
entries.relief: excluding or limiting the audio evidence

entries.title: Motion to Preclude Lay Medical Opinion by Police Witnesses
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to preclude any testimony by police witnesses offering lay medical opinions or injury causation testimony. Police witnesses are not qualified as medical experts and lack the requisite training, education, or experience to provide opinions on medical causation or the extent of injuries.
entries.relief: precluding all lay medical opinion and injury causation testimony by police witnesses

entries.title: Motion for Medical Records
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth to disclose whether the complainant was medically examined or treated in connection with the alleged incident, and to produce complete copies of all related medical and EMS records, including provider identity and facility information.
entries.relief: compelling production of all medical and EMS records related to the alleged incident

entries.title: Motion to Reveal Confidential Informant Identity
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth to provide the name and contact information of the confidential informant listed as a witness in the law enforcement reports, all police department files regarding the informant's contact with the Defendant, and the remuneration arrangements for the informant.
entries.relief: ordering the Commonwealth to reveal the identity and contact information of the confidential informant

entries.title: Motion to Be Furnished with Witness Criminal Records
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order directing the Commonwealth through the Criminal History Systems Board and/or the Commissioner of Probation to provide the criminal records of potential witnesses and/or individuals potentially implicated in this matter.
entries.relief: compelling production of criminal records for all listed witnesses

entries.title: Motion for Prior Complaints of Sexual Assault by Complainant
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order directing the Commonwealth to provide in writing the details of each previous accusation of sexual assault made by the complainant against any other person. Prior false allegations of sexual assault are admissible and exculpatory.
entries.relief: compelling the Commonwealth to disclose all prior complaints of sexual assault made by the complainant
authorities: Commonwealth v. Pyne, 35 Mass. App. Ct. 36 (1993)

entries.title: Motion for Production of Rape Kit Results
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order directing the Commonwealth to furnish copies of rape kit results regarding the alleged victim. These materials are directly relevant to the defense and subject to mandatory disclosure.
entries.relief: compelling production of all rape kit results and related forensic evidence

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Prior Domestic Incidents
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude evidence of prior domestic incidents, prior restraining orders, or prior 209A proceedings because such evidence is not relevant to the charged conduct and its admission would be unfairly prejudicial, confusing, and invite the jury to convict based on propensity rather than proof.
entries.relief: excluding all evidence of prior domestic incidents and related proceedings

entries.title: Motion to Compel Production of 209A Records and Orders
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to compel production of all 209A records, restraining orders, applications, and related court documents pertaining to the complainant and the Defendant. These records are material to the defense and may contain exculpatory information, prior inconsistent statements, or evidence bearing on the complainant's credibility.
entries.relief: compelling production of all 209A records and restraining order documentation

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Drug Certificate Without Expert Testimony
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude any drug certificate or certificate of analysis unless the Commonwealth produces the analyst for cross-examination. Admission of a drug certificate without live testimony from the analyst violates the Defendant's rights under the Confrontation Clause.
entries.relief: excluding all drug certificates unless the certifying analyst testifies at trial

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Lay Opinion on Value
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude lay opinion testimony regarding the value of any alleged stolen property. Valuation testimony requires proper foundation and, where specialized knowledge is required, must be given by a qualified expert.
entries.relief: excluding all lay opinion testimony regarding the value of alleged stolen property

entries.title: Motion to Compel Production of Surveillance Footage - Larceny
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to compel production of all surveillance video footage from any location relevant to the alleged larceny. This footage is material to the defense, may be exculpatory, and is subject to mandatory disclosure.
entries.relief: compelling production of all surveillance footage relevant to the alleged offense

entries.title: Motion to Suppress - Exit Order (MV Stop)
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence obtained after an unlawful exit order. Under Article 14 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights, a police officer may not order a driver to exit a lawfully stopped vehicle without a reasonable basis to believe that officer safety requires it or that criminal activity is afoot.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence obtained after the unlawful exit order

entries.title: Motion to Suppress - Inventory Search
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence obtained from an inventory search of the Defendant's vehicle because the search was not conducted pursuant to standardized police procedures, was pretextual, or was otherwise outside the scope of a lawful inventory search.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence obtained from the unlawful inventory search

entries.title: Motion for Disclosure of Police Witness Disciplinary, Credibility, and Impeachment Material
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for disclosure of all disciplinary, credibility, impeachment, and bias material concerning any police witness or law enforcement witness the Commonwealth may call at hearing or trial. This request includes sustained findings, pending or prior credibility concerns, dishonesty findings, report falsification issues, excessive force findings, evidence handling issues, bias complaints, impeachment material, prior inconsistent statements, and any other information favorable to the defense or material to cross examination.
entries.relief: ordering disclosure of police witness disciplinary, credibility, and impeachment material

entries.title: Motion for Disclosure of Witness Lists, Witness Statements, and Witness Criminal Records
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for disclosure of witness lists, witness statements, and witness criminal records to the extent required or permitted by rule, court order, or local practice. The request includes written statements, recorded statements, summarized oral statements, prior inconsistent statements, cooperation agreements, promises, benefits, pending cases, convictions, probation status, and other information bearing on witness credibility, bias, motive, perception, memory, or truthfulness.
entries.relief: ordering disclosure of witness lists, witness statements, and witness criminal records

entries.title: Motion to Compel Production and Preservation of Surveillance Footage
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth and investigating agencies to identify, preserve, and produce all surveillance footage relevant to the alleged incident. This includes police, municipal, business, residential, courthouse, hospital, school, parking lot, booking area, station house, and third party video that may show the alleged offense, the parties, witnesses, police response, scene conditions, timing, identification, injury, statements, or other material facts.
entries.relief: ordering production and preservation of all relevant surveillance footage

entries.title: Motion for Production and Preservation of CAD Logs, 911 Calls, Dispatch Audio, Radio
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for production and preservation of all police audio, video, dispatch, and incident timeline records connected to this case. This request includes CAD logs, 911 calls, dispatch audio, radio transmissions, body worn camera footage, cruiser mounted camera footage, incident chronology, call history, unit assignment logs, arrival and clearance times, transport records, booking related recordings, and any timestamps showing when officers were dispatched, arrived, made contact, detained, searched, arrested, transported, or cleared.
entries.relief: ordering production and preservation of CAD logs, 911 calls, dispatch audio, radio transmissions, BWC footage, CMC footage, and incident chronology

entries.title: Motion for Funds to Retain the Services of a Social Worker with Incorporated Affidavit
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) to retain the services of a licensed social worker. The services are necessary to assist the Defendant in locating, navigating, and enrolling in available social programs, community resources, and support networks. The Defendant has difficulty independently identifying and completing sign-up procedures for essential programs, making professional intervention necessary for successful placement and release planning. The social worker will assist with community- based programs, housing frameworks, mental health resources, applications, and registration requirements.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $2,500.00 to retain the services of a licensed social worker

entries.title: Ex Parte Motion for Funds to Retain an Expert Consultant in Police Procedures and
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed One Thousand Dollars ($1,000.00) to retain an expert consultant in police procedures and investigations. The consultant is necessary to review discovery materials for compliance with accepted police practices and statutory and constitutional standards; analyze officer decision-making involving stops, searches, arrests, questioning, and interrogation procedures; review police reports, search warrants, body-worn camera videos, cruiser-mounted camera videos, and surveillance videos; assist counsel in developing explanatory and impeachment strategies; and prepare for cross-examination of law enforcement officers.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $1,000.00 to retain an expert consultant in police procedures and investigations

entries.title: Motion for Funds to Hire a Fingerprint Expert
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) to retain a fingerprint expert to assist in the preparation of the case. The Defendant is indigent and without funds to pay for a fingerprint expert. A fingerprint expert is necessary for the Defendant to mount an adequate defense where the Commonwealth has produced fingerprint evidence in discovery and may seek to use it at trial. The requested funds are reasonable under the circumstances, and justice requires that the motion be allowed.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $2,500.00 to retain a fingerprint expert

entries.title: Motion for Funds to Hire a Bloodstain Pattern Analysis Expert
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Three Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($3,500.00) to retain a bloodstain pattern analysis expert to assist in the preparation of the defense. Specialized bloodstain pattern review may be necessary and justified to assess the physical evidence, the Commonwealth's theory, and issues relevant to motion practice, cross-examination, and trial preparation. The funds requested are reasonable under the circumstances, and justice requires that the motion be allowed.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $3,500.00 to retain a bloodstain pattern analysis expert

entries.title: Motion for Funds to Hire a Medical Expert
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00) to retain a medical expert. The Defendant is indigent and without funds to pay for a medical expert. A medical expert is necessary to review medical records provided to the defense, advise the defense, and potentially testify at trial. The expert is necessary for the preparation of an adequate defense, the funds requested are fair and not excessive, and justice requires that the motion be allowed.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $5,000.00 to retain a medical expert

entries.title: Motion for Funds to Secure the Services of a DNA Expert with Incorporated Affidavit
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00) to retain a DNA expert to examine DNA-related materials and advise the defense. The Defendant is indigent and without funds to pay for an independent expert. The Commonwealth has indicated that it possesses items that may be submitted for DNA testing. A DNA expert is necessary to assist the defense with DNA science, review and analysis of DNA evidence, and whether the evidence should be included or excluded. Without expert assistance, the Defendant will be severely prejudiced and unable adequately to prepare for trial.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $5,000.00 to retain a DNA expert

entries.title: Ex Parte Motion for Funds to Retain a Cyber, Cellphone, Computer, and Digital Evidence Expert
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) to retain the services of a cyber, cellphone, computer, and digital evidence expert. The Defendant is indigent and without funds to pay for such an expert. Without the benefit of such an expert, the Defendant will be severely disadvantaged in preparing the case for trial. The expert is necessary to review electronic materials from cell phones and other electronic devices. The funds requested are reasonable under the circumstances given the seriousness of the charges, and justice requires that the motion be allowed.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $2,500.00 to retain a cyber, cellphone, computer, and digital evidence expert

entries.title: Ex Parte Motion for Funds to Transcribe Interview Tapes
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00) to transcribe recorded interview tapes produced in discovery. The transcriptions are necessary for the preparation of a proper and adequate defense. Without the transcriptions, the Defendant will be at a decided disadvantage at trial. The Defendant is indigent and without funds to pay for the transcriptions. The requested funds are reasonable under the circumstances, and justice requires that the motion be allowed.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $5,000.00 to transcribe recorded interview tapes produced in discovery

entries.title: Ex Parte Motion for Funds to Retain Interpreter and Translation Services with Incorporated
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) to retain interpreter and translation services. The services are necessary to permit counsel to communicate effectively with the Defendant, interview witnesses, review foreign-language documents, audio, video, or messages, and prepare the case for motions, plea negotiations, hearings, and trial. Without interpreter and translation assistance, counsel cannot adequately investigate the case, review discovery, develop impeachment, advise the Defendant, or prepare an effective defense.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $2,500.00 to retain interpreter and translation services

entries.title: Motion for Funds to Secure the Services of an Independent Psychiatrist/Psychologist with
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order authorizing funds not to exceed Three Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($3,500.00) to retain an independent psychiatrist or psychologist to examine the Defendant regarding mental status. The requested clinician is necessary because counsel has observed issues with the Defendant’s ability to appreciate and analyze the charges, process information, maintain focus and concentration, and communicate in an organized manner about the matters under consideration. The Defendant’s mental condition may bear on competency, criminal responsibility, ability to communicate with counsel, ability to assist in the preparation of the defense, and whether mental health issues played a role in the alleged conduct. An independent assessment is necessary to permit counsel to evaluate these issues as part of a proper and comprehensive defense strategy.
entries.relief: authorizing funds not to exceed $3,500.00 to retain an independent psychiatrist or psychologist

entries.title: Motion to Discover Rape Trauma Syndrome and/or Post Traumatic Stress Syndrome Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves that this Court order the Commonwealth to reveal whether it intends to introduce expert testimony concerning the complainant having rape trauma syndrome and/or post traumatic stress syndrome. See Commonwealth v. Hudson, 417 Mass. 536, 631 N.E.2d 50 (1994). If so, the Defendant moves for an order allowing a defense expert to examine the complainant for the presence or absence of the syndrome. If the complainant refuses to submit to the examination, the Defendant moves to preclude any testimony concerning the syndrome or syndromes. This motion is brought pursuant to Mass. R. Crim. P. 14(a)(2), 14(b)(2)(B), and the law of the land clause of Article 12 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights, including equal protection and due process principles. Commonwealth v. Lyons, 397 Mass. 644, 646-647, 492 N.E.2d 1142, 1144-1145 (1986). See also People v. Wheeler, 151 Ill. 2d 298, 176 Ill. Dec. 880, 602 N.E.2d 826 (1992), and Ake v. Oklahoma, 470 U.S. 68, 79 (1985).
entries.relief: requiring disclosure of rape trauma syndrome and/or post traumatic stress syndrome expert evidence, allowing examination by a defense expert if such evidence will be offered, and precluding syndrome testimony if the complainant refuses examination
authorities: Article 12 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Identification
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress any out- of-court identification because the procedure used was unnecessarily suggestive, unreliable, or otherwise created a substantial risk of misidentification. The Court should conduct a pretrial evidentiary hearing and exclude the identification and any fruits of that identification unless the Commonwealth can establish admissibility under constitutional and common-law fairness principles.
entries.relief: suppressing all out-of-court identification evidence and its fruits
authorities: Article 12 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights

entries.title: Motion to Exclude In-Court Identification
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to preclude any in- court identification where the witness did not previously make a reliable identification or where any prior identification procedure was suggestive, unreliable, or suppressed. A first-time or tainted courtroom identification is inherently suggestive and risks inviting the jury to accept identification evidence without adequate reliability safeguards.
entries.relief: precluding any in-court identification lacking an independent reliable basis
authorities: Article 12 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Evidence Seized Pursuant to Search Warrant
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress all evidence seized pursuant to the search warrant because the affidavit failed to establish probable cause, failed to establish a sufficient nexus between the alleged criminal activity and the place or item searched, relied on stale or unreliable information, lacked particularity, or otherwise failed to satisfy Article 14 and Fourth Amendment requirements.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence seized pursuant to the defective search warrant

entries.title: Motion for Franks/Amral Hearing
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an evidentiary hearing because the warrant affidavit contains material false statements, reckless misstatements, or material omissions necessary to the probable cause determination. If the challenged information is excised or the omitted information is included, the affidavit fails to establish probable cause.
entries.relief: ordering a Franks/Amral evidentiary hearing and suppressing the warrant evidence if probable cause fails

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Cell Phone Search
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress evidence obtained from the search of a cellular telephone because the search was conducted without valid authority, exceeded the scope of any warrant or consent, lacked sufficient particularity, or permitted a general exploratory search of private digital information.
entries.relief: suppressing all evidence obtained from the unlawful cell phone search

entries.title: Motion to Suppress CSLI, GPS, and Location Data
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress historical or real-time location evidence, including CSLI, GPS data, tower dump data, or other tracking records, because the Commonwealth failed to obtain lawful authority supported by probable cause and particularity, or because the collection exceeded the authorized scope.
entries.relief: suppressing CSLI, GPS, tower dump, and other unlawful location evidence

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Jail Calls
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress jail call evidence because the Commonwealth cannot establish proper authentication, reliable speaker attribution, lawful acquisition, adequate notice, voluntariness, relevance, or a non-prejudicial basis for admission.
entries.relief: suppressing or excluding improperly obtained or unauthenticated jail call evidence

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Booking Statements
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress statements obtained during booking where questioning exceeded routine administrative booking, was reasonably likely to elicit incriminating responses, or occurred without valid Miranda warnings and waiver.
entries.relief: suppressing custodial statements obtained through interrogation disguised as booking questions

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Probable Cause
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss because the complaint, application, or indictment fails to establish probable cause as to each required element of the charged offense. A criminal charge that is not supported by probable cause is legally inadequate and cannot proceed.
entries.relief: dismissing the charge for lack of probable cause
authorities: Commonwealth v. Moore, 93 Mass. App. Ct. 73 (2018)

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss Pursuant to Rule 36
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss pursuant to Mass. R. Crim. P. 36 because the Commonwealth failed to bring the case to trial within the time required by the rule, or because prosecutorial delay and lack of diligence have prejudiced the defense and violated the Defendant's speedy trial rights.
entries.relief: dismissing the charges for violation of speedy trial rights

entries.title: Motion to Sever Counts
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to sever counts because the charged offenses are not properly joined or because joint trial would create unfair prejudice, confuse the issues, invite propensity reasoning, or prevent a fair determination of guilt on each count separately.
entries.relief: ordering separate trials on improperly or prejudicially joined counts

entries.title: Motion to Sever Defendants
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to sever defendants because a joint trial would create substantial prejudice through antagonistic defenses, co-defendant statements, spillover evidence, unequal evidence, or other circumstances preventing a fair trial.
entries.relief: ordering a separate trial from any co-defendant

entries.title: Motion for Disclosure of Giglio Material
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for disclosure of all Giglio and impeachment material, including police credibility information, disciplinary findings, pending charges, promises, benefits, bias, cooperation agreements, inconsistent statements, and any information affecting the reliability or credibility of Commonwealth witnesses.
entries.relief: compelling disclosure of all Giglio and witness credibility material
authorities: Matter of Grand Jury Investigation, 485 Mass. 641 (2020)

entries.title: Motion to Compel Rule 14 Discovery
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to compel complete Rule 14 discovery from the Commonwealth and the prosecution team, including all police reports, witness statements, expert materials, identification procedure records, physical evidence, digital evidence, and all information favorable to the defense.
entries.relief: compelling complete Rule 14 discovery from the Commonwealth and prosecution team

entries.title: Motion for Discovery Sanctions
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for sanctions because the Commonwealth failed to comply with discovery obligations or court orders. Appropriate relief may include a further discovery order, continuance, exclusion of evidence, adverse instruction, dismissal with or without prejudice, contempt, or other just relief.
entries.relief: imposing appropriate sanctions for discovery violations

entries.title: Motion for DiGiambattista Instruction
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for a DiGiambattista instruction because the Commonwealth seeks to introduce an alleged statement, admission, or confession that was not recorded, was only partially recorded, or was recorded under circumstances that do not fully capture the interrogation. The jury should be instructed to weigh the alleged statement with great caution and care.
entries.relief: requiring a cautionary instruction concerning unrecorded or partially recorded statements
authorities: Commonwealth v. Drummond, 76 Mass. App. Ct. 625 (2010)

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Consciousness of Guilt Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude alleged consciousness-of-guilt evidence because the conduct is ambiguous, minimally probative, unfairly prejudicial, or likely to invite speculation and improper inference. Evidence such as flight, nervousness, false statements, or failure to appear should not be admitted without a strong factual and legal foundation.
entries.relief: excluding alleged consciousness-of-guilt evidence or limiting its use

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Gang Affiliation Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude gang affiliation evidence because it is highly inflammatory, invites propensity reasoning, and risks unfair prejudice substantially outweighing any legitimate probative value. The Commonwealth should not be permitted to introduce gang references unless it establishes a specific, non-propensity purpose and a direct connection to a disputed issue in the case.
entries.relief: excluding gang affiliation evidence and related references

entries.title: Motion to Exclude Social Media, Rap Lyrics, and Artistic Expression
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to exclude social media posts, rap lyrics, music videos, images, and artistic expression offered to inflame the jury, suggest propensity, or associate the Defendant with violence or criminality without a direct and reliable connection to a material issue.
entries.relief: excluding prejudicial social media, rap lyric, music video, and artistic-expression evidence

entries.title: Motion in Limine to Exclude Uncharged Misconduct and Propensity Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves in limine to exclude prior bad acts, uncharged conduct, prior accusations, or other propensity evidence. Such evidence is inadmissible when offered to show bad character or criminal propensity and should be excluded where any probative value is outweighed by unfair prejudice.
entries.relief: excluding prior bad acts and propensity evidence

entries.title: Ex Parte Motion for Funds to Retain an Investigator
entries.theory: The Defendant moves ex parte for funds to retain an investigator. Investigative services are reasonably necessary to locate and interview witnesses, inspect relevant locations, review discovery, obtain records, develop impeachment, and assist counsel in preparing motions, plea negotiations, hearings, and trial. Without investigative assistance, counsel cannot provide as effective a defense as would be available to a person with financial means.
entries.relief: authorizing reasonable funds to retain an investigator

entries.title: Ex Parte Motion for Additional Expert Funds
entries.theory: The Defendant moves ex parte for additional expert funds because the original authorization has been exhausted or is insufficient to complete the work reasonably necessary to the defense. Additional funds are required for continued review, testing, consultation, report preparation, or testimony.
entries.relief: authorizing supplemental expert funds reasonably necessary to the defense

entries.title: Motion for Change of Venue
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for a change of venue because pretrial publicity, community prejudice, or other local circumstances create a substantial risk that the Defendant cannot receive a fair and impartial trial in the current county.
entries.relief: transferring venue to protect the Defendant's right to a fair and impartial jury

entries.title: Motion for Humane Practice Hearing
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for a humane practice hearing to determine whether any alleged statement, admission, or confession was voluntary. Before any such statement may be admitted, the Commonwealth must prove voluntariness beyond a reasonable doubt, and if admitted, the jury must be instructed that they may consider the statement only if they independently find it voluntary.
entries.relief: ordering a humane practice hearing and excluding involuntary statements

entries.title: Motion to Preserve and Produce Cellebrite Extraction Data
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to preserve and produce all Cellebrite, UFED, GrayKey, or other forensic extraction materials, including complete extraction reports, extraction logs, audit logs, hash values, tool versions, scope settings, warrant returns, chain of custody, and any notes or communications concerning the extraction or review of digital evidence.
entries.relief: preserving and producing complete digital forensic extraction data and related records

entries.title: Motion for Disclosure of Informant Identity
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for disclosure of the identity and related information concerning any informant whose information, participation, observations, or conduct was material to the investigation, probable cause, charged offense, identification, controlled purchase, or defense. Disclosure is required where the informant is a percipient witness, participant, or necessary source of exculpatory or impeachment evidence.
entries.relief: compelling disclosure of informant identity and related impeachment or exculpatory information

entries.title: Motion to Inspect Grand Jury Minutes
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for leave to inspect the grand jury minutes because the defense has a particularized need to review whether the evidence before the grand jury established probable cause, whether exculpatory evidence was withheld, whether misleading evidence was presented, and whether the integrity of the proceeding was impaired.
entries.relief: permitting defense inspection of relevant grand jury minutes and exhibits

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss for Prosecutorial Misconduct Before the Grand Jury
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss the indictment because misconduct, misleading evidence, omission of necessary exculpatory evidence, impairment of the grand jury process, or other irregularity undermined the integrity of the proceeding and created a substantial likelihood that the grand jury was improperly influenced.
entries.relief: dismissing the indictment due to impairment of the integrity of the grand jury proceeding

entries.title: Motion for Discovery and Production of Discoverable Information
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth to produce discoverable information under Mass. R. Crim. P. 14, including all statements of the Defendant and any co- defendant, alleged admissions by silence with the time, place, manner, and means of the alleged admission, witness statements, police reports, other relevant statements known to the prosecution, evidence of physical condition, evidence no longer in the prosecution's possession, prospective witness information, expert or opinion witness materials, and all exculpatory evidence. The requested discovery is necessary to investigate the case, prepare motions, test the Commonwealth's proof, develop impeachment, and prepare for trial.
entries.relief: compelling production of discoverable information, including statements, reports, witness information, expert materials, and exculpatory evidence

entries.title: Supplemental Motion for Specific Discovery and Production of Discoverable Information
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for supplemental discovery requiring the Commonwealth to disclose specific categories of information material to the defense, including prior records and pending cases of victims or prospective prosecution witnesses; prior misconduct, bad acts, drug sales, or drug purchases by such witnesses; threats, promises, inducements, rewards, immigration- related pressure, protection, money, or other benefits affecting testimony or cooperation; prior cooperation with law enforcement; relevant drug or alcohol ingestion; scientific tests that did not reveal evidence favorable to the prosecution; the details and sequence of any Defendant or co-defendant statements; any verbal acts requested of the Defendant or co-defendant; the seizure history and chain of physical evidence; other persons with relevant information not listed as witnesses; evidence of the victim's violence, threats, or reputation for violence; and notice of prior bad acts, prior convictions, charts, or summaries the Commonwealth intends to use.
entries.relief: compelling supplemental, itemized discovery material to impeachment, statements, physical evidence, witness credibility, victim violence, and notice issues

entries.title: Motion to Inspect Tangible Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth to permit defense counsel and any necessary defense representative to inspect, examine, photograph, copy, or otherwise document all tangible evidence, documents, photographs, physical exhibits, and related materials the Commonwealth intends to use at trial or that are material to the preparation of the defense.
entries.relief: allowing defense inspection, examination, photographing, and copying of tangible evidence and related trial materials

entries.title: Motion for Discovery of Medical Evidence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth to disclose whether any alleged victim or relevant witness was examined or treated by a doctor, hospital, clinic, emergency medical provider, or other medical professional in connection with the case. If so, the Defendant requests the name and address of the provider and production of the medical report, treatment record, injury documentation, photographs, or related medical evidence concerning the examination or treatment.
entries.relief: compelling disclosure and production of medical- provider information, medical reports, treatment records, injury documentation, and related medical evidence

entries.title: Motion for Production of People Interviewed by Law Enforcement Regarding This Case
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth to produce the names, addresses, telephone numbers, and available statements or interview information for all persons interviewed by law enforcement regarding this case who are not expected to be called as Commonwealth witnesses. Such persons may have observed relevant events or may possess exculpatory, impeachment, or defense-favorable information, and the Commonwealth will not be prejudiced by disclosure.
entries.relief: compelling production of identifying information and available interview information for non-called persons interviewed by law enforcement

entries.title: Motion for Exculpatory Evidence Concerning Details of Alleged Fresh Complaint
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring the Commonwealth to disclose the details of each occasion on which the complainant related that the Defendant sexually assaulted him or her. This includes the name and address of each person to whom the complaint was made, the relationship of that person to the complainant, the date, time, and location of each complaint, and the details of the complaint, including the nature of the alleged assault, the person or persons allegedly involved, and the circumstances preceding and following the alleged assault. The request includes complaints made to family members, friends, police, hospital personnel, counselors, therapists, or employees of the District Attorney's Office. Timing differences and inconsistencies in such complaints may constitute exculpatory and impeachment evidence and are necessary for any motion in limine regarding fresh complaint evidence.
entries.relief: compelling disclosure of the details, recipients, timing, location, and substance of each alleged fresh complaint
authorities: Commonwealth v. O'Brien, 27 Mass. App. Ct. 184 (1989)

entries.title: Motion for Rule 17 Summons of Non-Privileged Records
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for a summons requiring production of identified non-privileged records before trial. The requested records are evidentiary and relevant, are not otherwise reasonably procurable through due diligence, are necessary to permit proper preparation, and the request is made in good faith rather than as a general fishing expedition.
entries.relief: issuing a Rule 17 summons for production of identified non-privileged records

entries.title: Defendant's Demand to Produce Rule 14 Materials
entries.theory: The Defendant demands production of discoverable documents and evidence in the possession, custody, or control of the Commonwealth or prosecution team, including police reports, witness statements, 911 recordings, grand jury materials where applicable, photographs, recordings, tangible evidence, and other materials relevant to preparation of the defense.
entries.relief: ordering production of requested Rule 14 materials and related evidence

entries.title: Motion for Discovery After Refusal to Comply with Demand to Produce
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order compelling discovery where the Commonwealth has refused, failed, or declined to comply with a proper demand to produce. The requested materials are relevant, discoverable, and necessary for investigation, motion practice, impeachment, plea evaluation, and trial preparation.
entries.relief: compelling production of materials withheld after a demand to produce

entries.title: Motion for Protective Order Regulating Discovery
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for a protective order denying, conditioning, limiting, delaying, or regulating discovery where unrestricted disclosure would create unfair prejudice, invade privacy, expose privileged or sensitive material, endanger a person, compromise defense preparation, or otherwise require court supervision to protect the fairness of the proceeding.
entries.relief: entering a protective order regulating the timing, scope, or manner of discovery

entries.title: Motion for Required Finding of Not Guilty
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for required findings of not guilty because the Commonwealth's evidence is insufficient as a matter of law to prove each essential element of the charged offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Where the evidence leaves an element to conjecture or speculation, the case may not be submitted to the jury.
entries.relief: entering required findings of not guilty on legally insufficient charges

entries.title: Motion to Quash Grand Jury Subpoena
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to quash a grand jury subpoena where the subpoena is overbroad, unreasonable, improperly issued, seeks privileged or constitutionally protected material, imposes an undue burden, or is being used in a manner that exceeds the proper investigative function of the grand jury.
entries.relief: quashing or narrowing the grand jury subpoena
authorities: In re Grand Jury Subpoena, 454 Mass. 685 (2009)

entries.title: Petition for Writ of Habeas Corpus Ad Testificandum
entries.theory: The Defendant petitions for a writ of habeas corpus ad testificandum requiring the custodian of an incarcerated material witness to produce that witness for a scheduled hearing or trial. The witness is material and necessary to the defense, and production is required to protect the Defendant's right to present evidence.
entries.relief: issuing a writ requiring production of the incarcerated material witness

entries.title: Motion for Delivery of Property Seized Pursuant to Search Warrant
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an order requiring delivery or production of property seized pursuant to a search warrant when the property is needed for inspection, examination, testing, motion practice, trial preparation, or use at hearing or trial.
entries.relief: ordering delivery or production of seized property for defense inspection and use

entries.title: Motion to Modify Bail or Pretrial Release Conditions
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to modify bail or pretrial release conditions because the existing order is greater than necessary to assure appearance, does not adequately account for the Defendant's financial resources, community ties, history of appearance, ability to comply with conditions, and available less restrictive alternatives, or otherwise results in unnecessary pretrial detention.
entries.relief: modifying bail or release conditions and ordering release on reasonable terms

entries.title: Motion for Bond Review
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for review of the terms of pretrial release and for the Court to set a reasonable bond. The Defendant's community ties, family ties, residence history, lack of flight risk, ability to comply with court orders, and available conditions of release support a lower and reasonable bond.
entries.relief: setting a reasonable bond and appropriate conditions of pretrial release

entries.title: Motion for Release on Personal Recognizance
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for release on personal recognizance because the Defendant is not a flight risk, has community and family ties, can comply with all court orders, and conditions short of financial bail are sufficient to assure appearance and protect the integrity of the proceedings.
entries.relief: releasing the Defendant on personal recognizance or the least restrictive conditions necessary

entries.title: Demand for Probable Cause Hearing
entries.theory: The Defendant demands a probable cause hearing and does not waive that right. The Commonwealth must proceed expeditiously, provide notice to the Defendant and counsel, and establish probable cause for the charged offense rather than leaving the case pending without the hearing required by law.
entries.relief: scheduling a prompt probable cause hearing with proper notice to the Defendant and counsel

entries.title: Motion for Continuance
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to continue the scheduled hearing or trial date because additional time is necessary to review discovery, investigate facts, interview witnesses, prepare motions, consult with the Defendant, obtain necessary records or expert assistance, and provide effective assistance of counsel.
entries.relief: continuing the scheduled hearing or trial date in the interests of justice

entries.title: Defendant's Petition to Testify Before the Grand Jury
entries.theory: The Defendant petitions for permission to testify before any grand jury considering this matter and requests that the Commonwealth provide defense counsel notice of any scheduled grand jury proceeding concerning the case so the Defendant may exercise that request in a meaningful manner.
entries.relief: permitting the Defendant to testify before the grand jury and requiring notice of the scheduled proceeding

entries.title: Notice of Alibi
entries.theory: The Defendant gives notice of an alibi defense and identifies the place or places where the Defendant claims to have been at the time of the alleged offense, together with the witnesses the Defendant may call in support of that defense, subject to supplementation as investigation continues.
entries.relief: filing and serving notice of alibi and preserving the Defendant's right to present alibi evidence

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss Defective Indictment or Complaint
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss a defective indictment or complaint because the charging language fails to provide a plain, concise, and definite statement of the act alleged, omits an essential element, fails to charge an offense, or otherwise prevents the Defendant from receiving constitutionally adequate notice of the accusation.
entries.relief: dismissing the defective indictment, complaint, or count

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss and Release Defendant for Untimely Grand Jury Action
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss the case and for release where the Commonwealth has failed to take timely grand jury action or failed to provide the required probable cause hearing while the Defendant remains detained. The Defendant has not waived the probable cause hearing, and continued detention without timely action violates the Defendant's pretrial rights.
entries.relief: dismissing the case or ordering the Defendant's release due to untimely grand jury or probable cause action

entries.title: Notice of Appeal
entries.theory: The Defendant gives notice of appeal from the judgment of conviction, sentence, order, or other appealable ruling, and preserves the Defendant's right to appellate review of each part of the judgment or order identified in the notice.
entries.relief: filing and serving a notice of appeal from the identified judgment or order

entries.title: Motion for Extension of Time to File Notice of Appeal
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an extension of time to file a notice of appeal where a timely notice was not filed because of excusable neglect, good cause, counsel workload, transcript review, disruption in appellate preparation, or other circumstances warranting additional time.
entries.relief: extending the time for the Defendant to file a notice of appeal

entries.title: Motion for Extension of Time to File Defendant-Appellant's Brief
entries.theory: The Defendant-Appellant moves for additional time to file the appellate brief because the record is substantial, counsel has been diligently preparing the appeal, additional transcript or record review is necessary, or other work and case circumstances make the existing deadline impracticable.
entries.relief: granting additional time to file the Defendant- Appellant's brief

entries.title: Motion for Enlargement of Time to Perfect Appeal and Extend Stay
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to enlarge the time to perfect the appeal and, where applicable, to extend an existing stay of execution. Additional time is necessary because the appeal has not yet been perfected despite diligence, and the stay should remain in place to preserve meaningful appellate review.
entries.relief: enlarging the time to perfect the appeal and extending any stay of execution

entries.title: Motion for Stay of Execution Pending Appeal
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for a stay or suspension of execution of the judgment pending appeal and requests release on recognizance, reasonable bail, or other appropriate conditions. A stay is necessary to prevent irreparable harm and preserve the Defendant's ability to obtain meaningful appellate review.
entries.relief: staying execution of the judgment pending appeal and setting reasonable release conditions

entries.title: Motion for Appeal Bond
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for an appeal bond and stay of execution while appellate proceedings are pending. The appeal presents non-frivolous issues, enforcement of the judgment would cause serious harm, and reasonable bond or conditions will assure the Defendant's appearance.
entries.relief: setting an appeal bond and staying execution of the judgment pending appeal

entries.title: Application for Further Appellate Review
entries.theory: The Defendant applies for further appellate review of an Appeals Court decision because substantial reasons affecting the public interest, the interests of justice, settled law, or the fair administration of criminal cases warrant review by the Supreme Judicial Court.
entries.relief: granting further appellate review in the Supreme Judicial Court

entries.title: Motion for Reargument of Appellate Division Order
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for reargument or reconsideration of an appellate division order where the court overlooked or misapprehended controlling law, material facts, record evidence, constitutional claims, or issues necessary to a fair appellate decision.
entries.relief: granting reargument or reconsideration of the appellate division order

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss Commonwealth's Appeal
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss the Commonwealth's appeal where the appeal is not authorized, is untimely, lacks jurisdictional basis, seeks review of a nonappealable order, or otherwise should not proceed under governing appellate rules and constitutional protections.
entries.relief: dismissing the Commonwealth's appeal

entries.title: Motion to Withdraw Appeal
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to withdraw or voluntarily dismiss the pending appeal after consultation with counsel and a determination that dismissal is in the Defendant's interest or otherwise appropriate under the circumstances.
entries.relief: dismissing or withdrawing the Defendant's pending appeal

entries.title: Motion to Revise or Revoke Sentence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to revise or revoke the sentence because the sentence should be modified in light of the nature and circumstances of the offense, the Defendant's history and character, proportionality, newly presented mitigation, or other reasons showing that the sentence is unduly harsh or should be corrected.
entries.relief: revising, revoking, reducing, or otherwise modifying the sentence

entries.title: Motion to Set Aside Unauthorized or Invalid Sentence
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to set aside a sentence that was unauthorized, illegally imposed, or otherwise invalid as a matter of law. A sentence imposed contrary to statute, rule, constitutional requirement, or lawful sentencing authority must be vacated or corrected.
entries.relief: setting aside, vacating, or correcting the unauthorized or invalid sentence

entries.title: Motion to Set Aside and Vacate Verdict
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to set aside and vacate the verdict because legal error, constitutional violation, newly discovered evidence, juror issue, insufficiency, or other circumstances undermine the reliability of the verdict and require post-verdict relief.
entries.relief: setting aside and vacating the verdict or ordering a new trial

entries.title: Motion to Vacate Judgment
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to vacate the judgment because the conviction, restraint, or judgment was imposed in violation of the Constitution or laws of the United States or Massachusetts, the court lacked jurisdiction, newly discovered evidence warrants relief, or justice requires a new trial or other post- conviction remedy.
entries.relief: vacating the judgment, ordering a new trial, or granting appropriate post-conviction relief

entries.title: Motion to Vacate Judgment for Ineffective Assistance of Counsel
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to vacate the judgment and for a new trial because trial counsel's performance fell measurably below that expected of an ordinary fallible lawyer and likely deprived the Defendant of an otherwise available, substantial ground of defense or otherwise prejudiced the defense.
entries.relief: vacating the judgment and ordering a new trial based on ineffective assistance of counsel

entries.title: Motion for Writ of Error Coram Nobis
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for post-conviction relief in the nature of coram nobis because facts outside the record, newly discovered evidence, or other fundamental circumstances unknown at the time of judgment show that the conviction or judgment was obtained in violation of constitutional rights or should otherwise be vacated.
entries.relief: vacating the judgment or granting appropriate coram nobis relief

entries.title: Motion for Post-Conviction DNA Testing
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for post-conviction forensic or scientific analysis of evidence because the Defendant was convicted of a criminal offense, remains restrained by that conviction, asserts factual innocence, and the requested DNA or scientific testing could produce evidence material to the conviction or sentence.
entries.relief: ordering post-conviction DNA or forensic testing of identified evidence

entries.title: Motion to Release Unlawfully Detained Probationer
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for immediate release from custody where the Defendant is detained solely on an alleged probation violation and has not received the required timely initial violation hearing or other process necessary to justify continued detention.
entries.relief: releasing the Defendant from custody pending the probation violation hearing
authorities: Superior Court Guidelines for Probation Violation Proceedings

entries.title: Petition for Writ of Habeas Corpus
entries.theory: The Petitioner seeks habeas corpus relief because the detention is unlawful, the sentence has expired, custody is not supported by a lawful judgment or mandate, parole or probation custody is improper, or other circumstances require judicial inquiry into the cause of imprisonment or restraint.
entries.relief: issuing or sustaining a writ of habeas corpus and discharging the Petitioner from unlawful restraint

entries.title: Reply to Return of Habeas Corpus
entries.theory: The Petitioner replies to the return of habeas corpus by denying that the detention is lawful and asserting the factual and legal reasons why the judgment, mandate, parole warrant, sentence calculation, or other claimed basis for custody does not justify continued imprisonment or restraint.
entries.relief: sustaining the writ and discharging the Petitioner from unlawful restraint

entries.title: Defendant's Challenge to Entire Panel of Prospective Trial Jurors
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to strike the entire panel of prospective trial jurors where improper, prejudicial, or case- committing statements or questions were heard by the panel and the resulting prejudice cannot be cured by instruction or individual questioning. The integrity of jury selection requires dismissal of the panel and selection of an untainted venire.
entries.relief: striking the entire panel of prospective trial jurors and selecting an untainted panel

entries.title: Motion Objecting to Unsupported Jury Instructions
entries.theory: The Defendant objects to jury instructions on any charge, theory, element, lesser included offense, or factual basis unsupported by sufficient evidence. Where the Commonwealth has not introduced evidence sufficient to permit a rational jury to find the required elements beyond a reasonable doubt, the Court should decline the instruction and enter required findings where appropriate.
entries.relief: declining unsupported jury instructions and preserving the Defendant's objection

entries.title: Motion for Complete Recordation of Trial Proceedings
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for complete recordation and transcription of trial proceedings and related hearings so that testimony, objections, rulings, impeachment, and other material events are preserved for effective representation, confrontation, cross-examination, and appellate review.
entries.relief: ordering complete recordation and transcription of trial proceedings and related hearings

entries.title: Motion for Production of Grand Jury Minutes
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for production of the grand jury minutes and related exhibits necessary to determine whether the integrity of the grand jury proceedings was impaired, whether exculpatory evidence was withheld or distorted, and whether the indictment was supported by competent evidence.
entries.relief: ordering production of grand jury minutes and exhibits

entries.title: Motion to Dismiss Indictment for Impaired Grand Jury Integrity
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to dismiss the indictment because the Commonwealth impaired the integrity of the grand jury proceedings by presenting false, distorted, incomplete, or misleading evidence, withholding known exculpatory evidence, or otherwise creating an unfair and unreliable basis for indictment.
entries.relief: dismissing the indictment for impairment of grand jury integrity

entries.title: Motion for Exculpatory Grand Jury Material
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for disclosure of all exculpatory information known to the Commonwealth during the grand jury presentation, including evidence that would have materially affected the grand jury's decision to indict or undermined the reliability of the Commonwealth's theory.
entries.relief: requiring disclosure of exculpatory grand jury material

entries.title: Motion for Disclosure of Confidential Informant Identity
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for disclosure of the confidential informant's identity where the informant was a percipient participant, material witness, or necessary source of information for challenging probable cause, reliability, identification, possession, distribution, or police conduct.
entries.relief: ordering disclosure of the confidential informant's identity or appropriate in camera review

entries.title: Motion for Informant Reliability and Controlled Buy Records
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for production of informant reliability records, controlled-buy documentation, search records, buy-money records, debriefing notes, surveillance notes, photographs, audio or video recordings, promises, benefits, payments, criminal history, and impeachment material related to any informant relied upon by the Commonwealth.
entries.relief: compelling production of informant reliability, payment, impeachment, and controlled-buy records

entries.title: Motion to Suppress Evidence Based on Unreliable Informant Information
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress evidence obtained from informant-based police action because the Commonwealth failed to establish the informant's basis of knowledge and veracity, failed to corroborate material allegations, or relied on stale, conclusory, or unreliable information.
entries.relief: suppressing evidence obtained through unreliable informant-based information

entries.title: Motion to Traverse Search Warrant Affidavit
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to traverse the search warrant affidavit because the affidavit contains false statements, reckless misstatements, material omissions, conclusory assertions, or misleading descriptions that affected the probable cause determination.
entries.relief: ordering a traverse hearing and suppressing warrant evidence if probable cause fails

entries.title: Motion for Search Warrant Return, Inventory, and Execution Records
entries.theory: The Defendant moves for production of the complete search warrant package and execution records, including the application, affidavit, warrant, return, inventory, photographs, body camera footage, entry plan, operational notes, seizure logs, chain of custody records, and all reports concerning execution of the warrant.
entries.relief: compelling production of the complete search warrant package and execution records

entries.title: Motion to Suppress for Lack of Nexus in Search Warrant
entries.theory: The Defendant moves to suppress evidence seized pursuant to the search warrant because the affidavit failed to establish a sufficient nexus between the alleged criminal activity and the place or item searched. Suspicion that a person committed a crime does not itself establish probable cause to search a home, phone, vehicle, or other location.
entries.relief: suppressing evidence seized pursuant to a warrant lacking nexus
